name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: Ingredient-to-step reconciliation PASSED: all 20 locked lines are used, no step uses an unpurchased item.

Two separate salt commodities are intentional and both used: Sea Salt (spice rub 1 3/4 tsp + rice pot 3 1/2 tsp) and plain Salt (corn salad 1 scant tsp), matching the source's distinct 'sea salt' vs 'salt' calls.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn is one of those things that tastes like a splurge and costs like a side dish. Take the smoky, tangy, lime-hit flavor of elote off the cob, spoon it over cilantro lime rice and seared chicken, and you have a bowl that eats like takeout and preps like a champ. This is the kind of dinner that makes leftovers feel like a reward instead of a punishment.

Here is the honest part. It hits 44.6 grams of protein and 597 calories a serving, so it earns its spot as a real dinner, not a snack pretending to be one. You are getting seasoned chicken, a proper carbohydrate in the rice, and a corn salad that carries the whole thing. Fourteen containers, one cook, and a week where you already know what is for dinner.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the chicken breast in the biggest pack your store sells and cut it down yourself. Whole breasts are cheaper than anything pre-cut into strips or chunks, and cutting into 1-inch pieces takes about five minutes with a sharp knife.

Canned whole kernel corn is the move here, same as the original recipe. Drain it well so your salad does not go watery. Long-grain white rice out of the big bag is the cheapest carbohydrate on the shelf, and you already own most of the spice rub: chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder and onion powder are pantry regulars, so check what you have before you buy doubles.

Cotija is the one specialty item. A little goes a long way here since it is split between the salad and the topping, so one wedge covers the batch. If your store does not carry it, a firm queso fresco stands in fine. Greek yogurt and avocado oil mayo do the creamy work that heavy cream or sour cream would, without the extra fat load.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice, because it does its thing while you build everything else. Bring the water to a boil, stir in the rice and sea salt, then cover it, drop the heat to low and let it simmer about 20 minutes until tender. While it is still warm, fold in the chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice and lime zest so the rice drinks it all in.

Now the street corn salad. In a big bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you want the heat, chopped cilantro and the salt. Stir gently until it comes together, taste it, and adjust. Set it aside to let the flavors get acquainted.

For the chicken, mix the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and sea salt in a small bowl, then toss the chicken chunks in that rub until every piece is coated. Get a large skillet hot over medium heat with the olive oil, add the chicken, and cook about 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and reaches 165 degrees F inside. Do not crowd the pan, work in batches if you need to, or the chicken steams instead of searing.

To build, spread the warm cilantro lime rice across your containers, top with the chicken chunks, add a generous scoop of the street corn, then finish with cubed avocado, sliced red onion, a little more crumbled cotija, extra cilantro and a squeeze of fresh lime.
prose.portion_html:
This one splits across 14 containers, and the trick is to portion by weight, not by eyeball. Weigh your empty container, then weigh the full pot of rice, subtract, and divide by 14. That number is your rice-per-container target, and a kitchen scale keeps every box honest instead of the first few getting heaped and the last few getting robbed.

Rice on the bottom, then split the chicken evenly, then the corn salad. Hold the avocado, red onion, extra cotija and lime for serving day rather than packing them now, so the avocado does not brown and the garnish stays fresh. Land it right and every container clears 44.6 grams of protein at 597 calories.

Cook it once, and the payoff is 14 dinners already handled. No 6pm scramble, no delivery fee, no decision fatigue. The batch pays for itself in the meals you were about to buy some other, more expensive way.

And if you want the full board of recipes, the cost engine and every macro-checked card, membership runs a dollar a month. That is the cheapest line item in this whole plan.

steps: Make the cilantro lime rice: Bring the water to a boil, add the rice and sea salt, cover, reduce heat to low and simmer about 20 minutes until tender. Fold the warm rice with chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice and lime zest.

Make the street corn salad: In a bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, diced jalapeno if using, chopped cilantro and salt. Stir gently, taste, adjust and set aside.
Season the chicken: In a small bowl, mix the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and sea salt, then toss the 1-inch chicken chunks in the rub until coated.

Cook the chicken: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, add the chicken and cook about 4 to 5 minutes per side until cooked through and the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees F.

Assemble and portion: Divide the warm cilantro lime rice across the containers, top with chicken and a scoop of street corn, then finish with cubed avocado, sliced red onion, extra cotija, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
